title: Critical Flaw in Python’s Popular Pillow Image Library Allows Code Execution via a Crafted Image
summary: Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open.
card_summary: Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open.

sections.technical:
The flaw, CVE-2026-112900, is in the way Pillow handles EPS images, which it opens by passing the file's name to Ghostscript, a separate program it runs to turn the image into pixels, without checking the name first.

Referenced vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-112900.

email_summary: Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open. Tracked as CVE-2026-112900. Severity is rated critical.

title: Researchers Demonstrate Node2Shell RCE Exploit on Node.js Build Using Crafted Brotli Data

card_summary: Malicious Brotli data can make an application on an official build of Node.js run attacker-supplied code, security researchers at Imperva have demonstrated.

sections.technical:
Their "Node2Shell" proof of concept ran code on the official Node.js 24.22.0 image for Linux arm64, with no debugger or custom build, by feeding crafted data to the bundled Brotli decoder (CVE-2026-111497). Node.js disclosed the flaw

Referenced vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-111497.

title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
summary: CISA has added one new vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation.
card_summary: CISA has added one new vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation.

sections.impact:
CVE-2026-110447 Collabora Online – Built-in CODE Server OS Command Injection Vulnerability 

 
 This type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and poses significant risks to the federal enterprise. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied.

Assessed severity: CRITICAL.
sections.mitigation: BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities.
sections.context: This fits the broader data-exposure trend where follow-on abuse of leaked information is common.
